Houthis Sign Satellite Data Deals to Tighten Grip on Bab al-Mandab, Sources Say
The Houthis’ external intelligence apparatus has signed new agreements with a Chinese company to obtain satellite imagery and maritime surveillance data, intelligence sources told Sheba Intelligence.
The reported arrangements are aimed at expanding Houthi monitoring of commercial and military shipping across the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandab, Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea, with particular focus on Saudi and allied warships.
According to the sources, the data could support missile and drone operations by providing geographic coordinates, vessel movement and speed information. The agreements were reportedly brokered through Iran’s military attaché’s office in China, linking the Chinese company with Houthi liaison officers in Muscat.
The company was identified as Meentropy Technology (Hangzhou), operating as MizarVision. US Treasury records show the company was added to the sanctions list in May 2026 under Iran-related measures.
The agreements reportedly came after the Houthis expanded control along Yemen’s Red Sea coast to Dhubab and Mayun Island, increasing their ability to combine territorial control with satellite-based maritime surveillance around one of the world’s most strategic shipping chokepoints.
Sheba Intelligence could not independently verify whether the reported agreements are operational or confirm all details of the communications and targeting arrangements.
Full report available via the link in the comments
https://shebaintelligence.uk/houthis-sign-satellite-data-deals-to-tighten-grip-on-bab-al-mandab

🤖 Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and Sam Altman [Call](https://www.forbes.com/sites/gabrielalinzainescu/2026/09/13/anthropic-ceo-dario-amodei-calls-for-a-slowdown-in-frontier-ai/) For A Slowdown In Frontier AI
Dario Amodei has spent five years arguing that Anthropic could build frontier AI carefully and still win commercially. On Saturday he added a condition to that thesis: the whole industry has to ease off the accelerator.
In a roughly 3,900-word essay titled “We Must Pace the Frontier,” the Anthropic co-founder and CEO wrote that “we must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models.” He was explicit that pacing does not mean halting training or technical progress. It means building in enough time for alignment work, third-party verification and operational rigor to keep up with what the models can do.
Within hours, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman posted on X that “I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier,” adding that OpenAI would match Anthropic’s first commitment. Elon Musk’s reaction ran three words: “Dario is right.”
Amodei has been skeptical of slowdown calls before. In the essay he dismisses the 2023 “pause” letter as premature, because the models of that era could not act as coherent agents and there was little to study. He says two developments since the summer convinced him that the calculus has flipped.
📝: The only reason all the big AI CEOs are calling for a "slow down" in AI development are[ physical constraints](https://t.me/CIG_telegram/74215) in data center [construction](https://t.me/CIG_telegram/72989) and the maintenance of LLMs which need an ever increasing number of MWh to keep operating.
While they may cite cybersecurity as a reason, that hasn't stopped the development of LLMs until building data centers became impossible due to the price of raw materials (lack thereof) or opposition from the communities which were going to have to share local resources with the data centers.
Dario Amodei and Sam Altman's calls for the slow down of AI development "coincide" with China [restricting](https://t.me/CIG_telegram/83316) the export of rare earth metals necessary in data center construction, [memory chip shortages](https://t.me/CIG_telegram/76714), and a lack of energy production.
Already 5% of the U.S' energy output [is used to power](https://ourworldindata.org/data-insights/around-5-of-electricity-in-the-united-states-is-used-for-data-centers-far-more-than-the-global-average) existing data centers. The data center construction frenzy [may lead to as much as 25% the U.S' energy production](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-21/data-centers-on-track-to-suck-up-a-fifth-of-us-power-use-by-2035) being used to power data centers LLMs rely on. 
With the price of diesel skyrocketing and the looming threat of shortages of other petrochemical products which are used in the construction of data centers and computer chips, the resources to maintain the AI boom just aren't available anymore so the AI companies need an excuse to scale back and the excuse they've decided on is the "AI doomsday" shtick to show how "responsible" Amodei and Altman are with their toys.
🔗 https://www.forbes.com/sites/gabrielalinzainescu/2026/09/13/anthropic-ceo-dario-amodei-calls-for-a-slowdown-in-frontier-ai/

🔥🇸🇦 Houthis wreak havoc on Saudi oil artery
Saudi Arabia’s strategic East–West oil pipeline was shut down as a precaution after multiple drone strikes hit facilities in the Riyadh and Medina regions, according to the Saudi Energy Ministry.
Satellite imagery shows major fire and structural damage at pumping stations near Al-Masbah and Al-Dhahrah, with smoke and heat signatures detected along the pipeline corridor.
The 1,200-km Petroline can move around 7 million barrels per day from Abqaiq to the Red Sea port of Yanbu — a crucial alternative route while shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains restricted.
Saudi authorities say the attacks caused injuries and material damage. Riyadh’s preliminary assessment says the drones came from Iraq, while Iraqi authorities said they were launched from Maysan province.

🇸🇦 Key Saudi pipeline disruption cripples global oil supply
Global oil supply could decrease by up to 4% if Saudi Arabia’s major pipeline that delivers crude to the Red Sea coast does not resume operation soon, Reuters claims.
👉 The pipeline previously allowed the Saudis to mitigate the effect of the Strait of Hormuz blockade by funneling about 4 million barrels of oil daily to the port of Yanbu.
On September 11, however, the pipeline was shut down following Houthi drone strikes, and repairs may take up to six weeks, whereas Yanbu has no more than seven days’ worth of oil export stocks.
📍 The Houthis ability to de facto control maritime traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait further complicates Saudi oil exports via that route.

events.text:
🌏💵 How BRICS Grain Exchange moves to break West’s grip on Global South’s food markets
The Global South grows nearly half the world’s grain - yet still dances to the West’s price signals. 
BRICS’ ambitious grain plan aims to change that.
The BRICS Summit in New Delhi has backed further work on a Russia-championed Grain Exchange, first proposed in 2023 by Russia's Union of Grain Exporters and Producers, and supported by Russia’s president Putin.
Initially, Russia mulled a physical grain hub in Dubai, which envisioned large shipments stored in the UAE and then re-exported in batches across the Middle East and Africa. Liberal free-zone rules and Dubai’s logistics strength made the location attractive. 
Similar ideas were floated with Egypt and Bahrain. 
Overtime, the focus shifted from storage silos to a more institutional solution that resonates strongly across the Global South - a trading platform that gives members control over their own commodity flows.
➡️BRICS countries already produce around 1.24 billion tons of grain a year - roughly 44 % of the global total - and consume almost the same volume
➡️For wheat the share is even higher: 48 % of production and 47 % of consumption
➡️Russia, Brazil, India and China dominate the supply side; China, Egypt, Iran and many African nations sit on the demand side
➡️At the same time, prices, benchmarks and most of the trading infrastructure remain controlled by Western exchanges and intermediaries
The BRICS Grain Exchange is mulled as a single digital platform where producers and buyers can deal directly, settle in local currencies, use insurance/reinsurance mechanisms that Russia has also proposed, and set prices according to real intra-bloc supply and demand.
Key advantages:
🌏rules out extra middlemen inflating costs 
🌏lower margins and fairer prices for both farmers and consumers 
🌏for import-dependent nations in Africa, the Middle East and Asia - reduced dependence on the weaponized dollar; Western financial institutions 
🌏 greater resilience against supply shocks and political pressure 
🌏 the foundation that can later cover fertilizers, oilseeds and other essentials 
Forward-looking hybrid possibilities remain potentially possible, such as combining the exchange with physical storage and logistics hubs in strategic locations like the UAE, Egypt (a major buyer of Russian grain), ports along the International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC), the Northern Sea Route (actively being developed by Russia and China as a strategic Arctic route), or African gateways.
Russia estimates put the potential trading volume of such an exchange above $1 trillion, with annual savings of around $2.5 billion by cutting out biased benchmarks.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |

🇺🇸✈️ US fighter pilots are being grounded out of combat readiness
American fighter pilots are getting so little time in the cockpit that many are nowhere near the historically considered necessary sortie rates, reports the Military Times.
🔴 nondeployed fighter pilots are reportedly getting about one sortie a month thanks to budget reallocations and a crumbling maintenance infrastructure (Mitchell Institute data)
🔴 the number is down from roughly 5.5 sorties in fiscal 2023 - 60% of the required standard of 9-10 sorties for combat readiness
🔴 official pilot shortage stands at around 2,000 
🔴 former Air Force Secretary Frank Kendall redirected funding for 6,000 aviation maintenance positions in fiscal 2025
🔴 for Operation Epic Fury against Iran, the US could only muster 25 squadrons (about 325 aircraft)
🔴 that is roughly half the air power the Air Force alone deployed during Desert Storm in 1991 of the Air Force’s 1,084 aircraft in the active inventory, only 634 were mission capable in fiscal 2024
